introduction_markdown: Multiple choice paper (0510 Biology 1, June 2023, Ordinary Level, General Certificate of Education Board). Duration: one and a half hours. Answer ALL 50 questions; all questions carry equal marks. Each question has four suggested answers A, B, C and D; select only one answer for each question. If more than one answer is marked, the question scores zero. Non-programmable calculators are allowed.
enonce_intro_markdown: **Multiple choice questions** - choose the one correct answer, A, B, C or D. Section I (questions 1-7): independent questions. Section II (questions 8-20): biological diagrams. Section III (questions 21-25): one or more responses correct. Section IV (questions 26-30): pairs of statements. Section V (questions 31-40): lettered headings and a description. Section VI (questions 41-50): biological situations.

questions.enonce_markdown:
*SECTION I - directions as printed, summarised:* Each of these questions or incomplete statements is followed by four suggested answers. Select the best answer in each case and mark the answer sheet appropriately.

An organism which stores food in the pyrenoid.
questions.corrige_markdown: A pyrenoid is a protein body inside the chloroplast of green algae where starch is made and stored. Spirogyra is a filamentous green alga with spiral chloroplasts containing pyrenoids. Bacteria have no chloroplasts, Amoeba is an animal-like protozoan, and fungi have no chloroplasts and store glycogen. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Where does deamination occur in the body?
questions.corrige_markdown: Deamination is the removal of the amino group ($-\mathrm{NH_2}$) from excess amino acids. It takes place in the liver, producing urea (from the amino group) and a carbohydrate residue that is used for energy. The kidney only excretes the urea afterwards, which is the common trap. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: What is the effect of untreated sewage in water?
questions.corrige_markdown: Untreated sewage is rich in nitrates and phosphates. These nutrients make algae multiply quickly (an algal bloom); when the algae die, bacteria decompose them and use up the dissolved oxygen, which is eutrophication. Oxygen content falls, so B is the opposite of what happens. Option A describes only the first stage and not the effect on the water as a whole, and turbidity (C) is only a side effect. **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: Increases the population of aquatic organisms.

questions.enonce_markdown: Where in the nephron is glucose reabsorbed?
questions.corrige_markdown: All the glucose filtered into the Bowman's capsule is reabsorbed by active transport in the proximal convoluted tubule, so none is found in the urine of a healthy person. The loop of Henle reabsorbs water and salts, the distal tubule adjusts salts and water, and the collecting duct reabsorbs water under ADH. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: In the water cycle which process causes water molecules to return to the atmosphere?
questions.corrige_markdown: Evaporation (from oceans, lakes and soil, together with transpiration from plants) turns liquid water into water vapour that enters the atmosphere. Condensation changes vapour into droplets in the air, and precipitation brings water down to the Earth as rain. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of these prevents contraction of the uterine wall during pregnancy?
questions.corrige_markdown: Progesterone, secreted first by the corpus luteum and then by the placenta, maintains the thick lining of the uterus and inhibits contraction of the uterine muscle so that the foetus is not expelled early. Oestrogen stimulates growth of the uterine lining, and LH and FSH are pituitary hormones acting on the ovary. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The following organisms make up a food chain: snake, man, frog, locust, groundnut plant. Which of these is a primary consumer?
questions.corrige_markdown: The chain is groundnut plant, then locust, then frog, then snake, then man. A primary consumer feeds directly on the producer (the plant); the locust eats the groundnut plant, so it is the primary consumer. The frog is a secondary consumer and the snake a tertiary consumer. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
*SECTION II - directions as printed, summarised:* This group of questions relates to biological diagrams. Select the best answer for each question.

Which blood vessel carries deoxygenated blood from the heart to the lungs?
questions.corrige_markdown: The pulmonary artery leaves the right ventricle carrying deoxygenated blood to the lungs. This is the exception to the rule that arteries carry oxygenated blood. The pulmonary vein carries oxygenated blood back to the left atrium, and the renal vessels go to and from the kidneys. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Below is the diagram of an animal cell.

![fig-1](gce-ol-biology-2023-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_1.png)

Which numbered structure controls all the activities of the cell?
questions.corrige_markdown: Structure 3 is the nucleus (the round body with a dark nucleolus in the middle of the cell). The nucleus contains the chromosomes with the genes, so it controls all the activities of the cell, including protein synthesis and cell division. Structure 1 is the cell membrane, and 2, 4 and 5 are cytoplasmic structures such as vacuoles and mitochondria. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following parts of a flower make up the stamen?
questions.corrige_markdown: The stamen is the male part of the flower: the anther, which produces pollen, carried on a stalk called the filament. The stigma and style belong to the carpel (the female part), so B, C and D each mix male and female parts. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
![fig-2](gce-ol-biology-2023-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_2.png)

Which numbered structure(s) in the diagram of the fish control rolling and yawing?
questions.corrige_markdown: In the diagram 1 is the dorsal fin, 2 the lateral line, 3 the caudal (tail) fin, 4 the anal fin, 5 a pectoral fin, 6 a pelvic fin and 7 the operculum. The median (unpaired) dorsal and anal fins act like the keel of a boat: they stop the fish from rolling sideways and from yawing (swinging from side to side). The caudal fin is for propulsion, and the paired pectoral and pelvic fins control pitching, steering and braking. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Where in the digestive system of man is hydrochloric acid produced?
questions.corrige_markdown: Hydrochloric acid is secreted by the gastric glands of the stomach wall. It kills bacteria in food and gives the low pH (about 2) at which pepsin works best. The liver makes bile, and the ileum and colon do not produce acid. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
In which numbered structure of the villus are fatty acids and glycerol transported?

![fig-3](gce-ol-biology-2023-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_3.png)

*Options as printed:* A) 2.   B) 3.   C) 4.   D) 5.
questions.corrige_markdown: Fatty acids and glycerol are absorbed into the epithelium, recombined into fats and then carried away by the **lacteal**, the blind-ended lymph vessel of the villus, not by the blood capillaries (which take up glucose and amino acids). In the printed drawing 1 is the epithelium, 4 and 5 are vessels at the base of the villus, and the lacteal is either the central tube (3) or the dotted chain of vessels beside it (2). The scan is too schematic to say which one the examiner labelled, so the question is left open for self-assessment. Most probable intended key: **B** (3, the central lacteal).

questions.enonce_markdown: Which structure in the mammalian brain is concerned with involuntary and reflex activities?
questions.corrige_markdown: The medulla oblongata controls involuntary activities such as heart rate, breathing, swallowing, vomiting, coughing and sneezing. The cerebellum controls balance and coordination of muscles, the cerebrum controls voluntary actions, thinking and memory, and the hypothalamus controls body temperature and water balance. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Water enters a germinating seed through the:
questions.corrige_markdown: The micropyle is the tiny pore in the testa left where the pollen tube entered the ovule. Water enters the dry seed through it first, then the seed swells. The testa is the waterproof coat, the hilum is the scar where the seed was attached to the fruit, and the cotyledon stores food. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Where does implantation take place in the female reproductive system?
questions.corrige_markdown: After fertilisation in the oviduct (Fallopian tube) the zygote divides as it moves down, and the embryo sinks into the thick, vascular uterine lining (the endometrium) about 7 days later. This is implantation, so it takes place in the uterus. Oviduct and Fallopian tube are the same organ, which is where fertilisation, not implantation, occurs. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
The diagram below shows the position of endocrine glands in man:

![fig-4](gce-ol-biology-2023-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_4.png)

Which numbered structure secretes adrenaline?
questions.corrige_markdown: Adrenaline is secreted by the adrenal glands, which sit on top of the kidneys. In the diagram, 1 is the pituitary gland, 2 the thyroid, 3 an adrenal gland (above the kidney), 4 the gonads (testes or ovaries) and 5 the pancreas. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Below is the diagram of the fore arm.

![fig-5](gce-ol-biology-2023-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_5.png)

What happens during stretching of the arm?

*Options as printed:* A) 3 contracts and 7 also contracts.   B) 3 relaxes and 7 contracts.   C) 3 contracts and 7 relaxes.   D) 3 relaxes and 7 also relaxes.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The two muscles are an antagonistic pair: muscle 7 (on the front, attached to the shoulder blade 2 by tendon 1) is the biceps, and muscle 3 (on the back) is the triceps. To stretch (extend) the arm, the triceps (3) contracts and pulls the forearm straight while the biceps (7) relaxes. In bending, the opposite happens. The two muscles never contract together (A) or relax together (D) during a movement.

**Intended answer: C (3 contracts and 7 relaxes).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: Refraction of light rays in the eye follows this order:
questions.corrige_markdown: Light enters the eye and passes through the cornea (which bends it most), then the aqueous humour, the lens (fine focusing), and the vitreous humour before reaching the retina. D is the only option that follows this order. **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: Cornea, lens, aqueous humour, vitreous humour.
Cornea, vitreous humour, lens, aqueous humour.
Lens, aqueous humour, Cornea, vitreous humour.
Cornea, aqueous humour, lens, vitreous humour.

questions.enonce_markdown: Which structure in the mammalian skin is sensitive to pressure?
questions.corrige_markdown: Pacinian corpuscles, deep in the dermis, detect pressure (and vibration). Meissner's corpuscles detect light touch, and the hair plexus responds to hair movement. The commonest trap is Meissner's corpuscles (touch rather than pressure). **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
*SECTION III - directions as printed, summarised:* For each of the questions below, ONE or MORE of the response(s) is (are) correct. Decide which of the response(s) is (are) correct. Then choose: A if 1, 2 and 3 are all correct; B if 1 and 2 only are correct; C if 2 and 3 only are correct; D if 1 only is correct.

A solution with the same water potential as its surrounding can be described as:

1. Isotonic.
2. Hypertonic and hypotonic.
3. Hypotonic and isotonic.
questions.corrige_markdown: Two solutions with the same water potential (same concentration of solutes) are isotonic to each other, so there is no net movement of water between them. Hypertonic means a higher solute concentration (lower water potential) and hypotonic a lower solute concentration, so statements 2 and 3 describe unequal solutions. Only 1 is correct. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
In which form(s) do plants obtain nitrogen from the soil?

1. Nitrates.
2. Nitrites.
3. Ammonium compounds.

*Options as printed:* A) If 1, 2 and 3 are all correct.   B) If 1 and 2 only are correct.   C) If 2 and 3 only are correct.   D) If 1 only is correct.
questions.corrige_markdown: Plants absorb most of their nitrogen as **nitrates** (1), and some as **ammonium compounds** (3); nitrites (2) are toxic in quantity and are quickly oxidised to nitrates by nitrifying bacteria, so strictly the correct statements are 1 and 3. That pair is not among the four printed combinations, so a strict key does not exist. Many school textbooks, however, list nitrates, nitrites and ammonium salts together as the nitrogen compounds of the soil, which would give A, and some examiners would accept D (nitrates only). Because the key is doubtful, this question is left open for self-assessment. Most probable intended key: **A**.

questions.enonce_markdown:
An insect pollinated flower has:

1. Feathery stigma.
2. Brightly coloured petals.
3. Sticky pollen grains.
questions.corrige_markdown: Insect-pollinated flowers have brightly coloured petals to attract insects (2) and sticky or spiny pollen grains that stick to the insect's body (3). A feathery stigma (1) is a feature of wind-pollinated flowers, which have a large surface to catch light dry pollen; an insect-pollinated flower has a small, sticky stigma. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
What makes the alveolus a good respiratory surface?

1. It is highly permeable.
2. It is highly vascularized.
3. It has a thick epithelium.
questions.corrige_markdown: The alveolus is permeable to oxygen and carbon dioxide (1) and is surrounded by a dense network of blood capillaries (2) that carry gases away and keep the concentration gradient steep. Its epithelium is only one cell thick, so 3 (thick epithelium) is the opposite of the real feature: a thick wall would slow diffusion. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Arteries can be distinguished from veins in that:

1. Arteries carry blood at higher pressure than veins.
2. Arteries have thicker walls than veins.
3. Arteries have many values than veins.
questions.corrige_markdown: Arteries carry blood away from the heart at high pressure (1) and have thick, muscular, elastic walls to withstand it (2). Valves (the printed word is "values", a misprint for valves) are found in veins, not arteries (except at the base of the aorta and the pulmonary artery), so 3 is false. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
*SECTION IV - directions as printed, summarised:* Each of the following questions consists of a statement in the left-hand column followed by a second statement in the right-hand column. Choose your answer A, B, C or D as explained on the table: A if both are true and the 2nd statement is a correct explanation of the first; B if both are true and the 2nd statement is NOT a correct explanation of the first; C if the first is true and the second false; D if the first is false and the second true.

**First statement:** Glucose is completely broken down during aerobic respiration.

**Second statement:** The end products of aerobic respiration are more toxic.
questions.corrige_markdown: The first statement is true: in aerobic respiration glucose is fully oxidised to carbon dioxide and water, releasing the maximum energy. The second statement is false: carbon dioxide and water are harmless, less toxic than the end products of anaerobic respiration (lactic acid or ethanol). So the first is true and the second false. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: True, True: the 2nd statement is a correct explanation of the first.
True, True: the 2nd statement is NOT a correct explanation of the first.

questions.enonce_markdown:
**First statement:** The anopheles mosquito transmits Plasmodium.

**Second statement:** Anopheles mosquito feeds on the blood of its host causing malaria.

*Options as printed:* A) True, True: the 2nd statement is a correct explanation of the first.   B) True, True: the 2nd statement is NOT a correct explanation of the first.   C) True, False.   D) False, True.
questions.corrige_markdown: The first statement is true: the female Anopheles mosquito is the vector that carries the parasite Plasmodium from person to person. The second statement is also broadly true (the mosquito feeds on blood and malaria results), but strictly it is the Plasmodium injected during feeding that causes malaria, not the feeding itself, and the wording is loose. Because the second statement can be read either as the explanation of how Plasmodium is transmitted (A) or as an inaccurate or merely related statement (B), two keys are defensible and the question is left open for self-assessment. Most probable intended key: **A**.

questions.enonce_markdown:
**First statement:** In a food web, each organism has more than one food source.

**Second statement:** A food web is made up of several food chains.
questions.corrige_markdown: Both statements are true. A food web is a set of interconnected food chains, and because the chains overlap, an organism can feed on (and be eaten by) several others, so each has more than one food source. The second statement therefore explains the first. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: True, True: the 2nd statement is a correct explanation of the first.
True, True: the 2nd statement is NOT a correct explanation of the first.

questions.enonce_markdown:
**First statement:** During photosynthesis, light energy is converted to chemical energy.

**Second statement:** Green plants combine carbon dioxide and water using solar energy to produce organic food.
questions.corrige_markdown: Both statements are true. In photosynthesis chlorophyll traps light energy, which is used to build glucose from carbon dioxide and water; the energy ends up stored as chemical energy in the organic food. The second statement describes how the conversion occurs, so it explains the first. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: True, True: the 2nd statement is a correct explanation of the first.
True, True: the 2nd statement is NOT a correct explanation of the first.

questions.enonce_markdown:
**First statement:** The cell wall in a plant cell is made up of chitin.

**Second statement:** Cellulose provides roughage and prevents constipation in human diet.
questions.corrige_markdown: The first statement is false: the plant cell wall is made of cellulose, while chitin forms the cell walls of fungi and the exoskeleton of arthropods. The second statement is true: cellulose is dietary fibre (roughage), which adds bulk and keeps food moving through the gut. First false, second true. **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: True, True: the 2nd statement is a correct explanation of the first.
True, True: the 2nd statement is NOT a correct explanation of the first.

questions.enonce_markdown:
*SECTION V - directions as printed, summarised:* Each question consists of four lettered headings A, B, C, D. Select the heading which is closely related to the description which follows.

Select the heading which is closely related to the description: destroys leaves of plants through the formation of acid rain.
questions.corrige_markdown: Sulphur dioxide (from burning fossil fuels) dissolves in rain water to form sulphurous and sulphuric acid, which is acid rain and damages leaves. Carbon dioxide contributes to global warming, carbon monoxide is a poisonous gas that binds haemoglobin, and chlorofluorocarbons destroy the ozone layer. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Select the heading which is closely related to the description: selectively controls materials entering and leaving the cell.
questions.corrige_markdown: The cell membrane is partially (selectively) permeable and controls which substances enter and leave the cell. The cellulose cell wall is fully permeable and only gives support, the nucleus controls cell activities, and the chloroplast carries out photosynthesis. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Select the heading which is closely related to the description: plays a vital role in the regulation of blood glucose level.
questions.corrige_markdown: The pancreas contains the islets of Langerhans, which secrete insulin (lowers blood glucose) and glucagon (raises it). The salivary and gastric glands produce digestive juices, and the kidney excretes excess glucose only when the blood level is far too high (diabetes). **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Select the heading which is closely related to the description: causes uterine contractions during labour.
questions.corrige_markdown: Oxytocin, from the posterior pituitary, makes the uterine muscles contract strongly during labour (and also stimulates milk ejection). Progesterone does the opposite by relaxing the uterus, oestrogen builds the uterine lining, and testosterone is the male sex hormone. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Select the heading which is closely related to the description: contributes to the extension of the fore limb.
questions.corrige_markdown: The elbow is the hinge joint of the fore limb (arm): the forearm is bent and straightened (extended) there by the biceps and triceps. The hip and knee belong to the hind limb (leg), and the wrist is a joint between the forearm and the hand. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Select the heading which is closely related to the description: an inactive form of an enzyme produced in the stomach.
questions.corrige_markdown: Pepsinogen is secreted by the gastric glands and activated by hydrochloric acid into pepsin, which digests proteins. This protects the stomach lining from digesting itself. Trypsinogen is the inactive enzyme of the pancreas (not the stomach), androgen is a hormone and glycogen is a storage carbohydrate. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Select the heading which is closely related to the description: an example of a social insect.
questions.corrige_markdown: Honey bees live in organised colonies with a queen, workers and drones, each with its own job, which is social life. Mosquitoes, cockroaches and houseflies live as individuals. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Select the heading which is closely related to the description: are viviparous.
questions.corrige_markdown: Viviparous animals give birth to live young that develop inside the mother. Almost all mammals are viviparous (apart from the egg-laying monotremes). Birds are oviparous, most reptiles and fish lay eggs, so mammals is the best answer (a few fish and reptiles are viviparous, but this is not the general rule). **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Select the heading which is closely related to the description: relationship between rhizobium and leguminous plant.
questions.corrige_markdown: Rhizobium bacteria live in root nodules of legumes: they fix atmospheric nitrogen into compounds the plant can use, and the plant gives them carbohydrates and shelter. Both partners benefit, which is mutualism (symbiosis). **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Select the heading which is closely related to the description: converts soil nitrates into atmospheric nitrogen.
questions.corrige_markdown: Denitrifying bacteria (for example Pseudomonas) change nitrates in waterlogged soil into nitrogen gas, which returns to the air. Nitrosomonas turns ammonia into nitrites and Nitrobacter turns nitrites into nitrates (nitrification), and Azotobacter fixes nitrogen into the soil. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
*SECTION VI - directions as printed, summarised:* This group of questions deals with biological situations. Each situation is followed by a set of questions. Select the best answer for each question.

In an experiment to measure the rate of water uptake, a leafy shoot is cut under water and the cut end fitted into a rubber tubing of the potometer. Why was the shoot cut under water?
questions.corrige_markdown: If a shoot is cut in air, air is drawn into the cut xylem vessels and forms bubbles (an air lock) that break the continuous water column and block the uptake of water. Cutting under water keeps the xylem full of water, so the potometer reading is reliable. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: To prevent the leaves from drying.
To prevent air bubbles entering the xylem vessels.
To enable the shoot take in enough water.
To enable the shoot remain fresh throughout the experiment.

questions.enonce_markdown: In a demonstration to find out the food sample being tested, 1 cm$^3$ of dilute sodium hydroxide solution was added to 3 cm$^3$ of test sample drop wise. The test tube was shaken thoroughly. A purple colour was observed at the end. Which food substance was being tested and what is the name of the test?
questions.corrige_markdown: Sodium hydroxide followed by a drop of dilute copper sulphate solution gives a violet (purple) colour when protein is present: this is the Biuret test. Millon's test gives a red or pink colour, and the fat tests (Sudan III, osmic acid) give a red stain or a black colour, not purple. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A couple both have blood group AB. What percentage of the offspring will have the same blood group AB as their parents?
questions.corrige_markdown: Both parents are $I^A I^B$. The gametes are $I^A$ or $I^B$ from each parent, so the offspring are $I^A I^A$ (group A) 25%, $I^A I^B$ (group AB) 50% and $I^B I^B$ (group B) 25%. Group AB is 50%. Group O is impossible. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: In testing a leaf for starch, a leaf from a green plant that has been exposed to sunlight for at least 5 hours was detached and dipped in boiling water for 30 seconds. Why was the leaf dipped in boiling water for 30 seconds?
questions.corrige_markdown: Boiling water kills the cells (the protoplasm), which stops all enzyme action so no more starch is made or broken down, and it makes the cell membranes permeable so that iodine can enter. Chlorophyll is removed afterwards with hot ethanol (A), and boiling would destroy, not activate, enzymes. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: In an experiment to find out if heat is given off by germinating seeds. The seeds were initially soaked in water for 24 hours and later soaked for 15 minutes in sodium oxo chlorate and then rinsed in water. Why were the seeds soaked in oxo chlorate?
questions.corrige_markdown: Sodium oxochlorate (chlorate(I), like bleach) is a disinfectant. It kills fungi and bacteria on the surface of the seeds; otherwise their respiration would also release heat and make the result unreliable (the heat must come only from the seeds). The seeds are then rinsed so the chemical does not harm them. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: To increase the rate of germination.
To kill fungal spores on the grains.
To prevent oxygen entering the seeds.
To absorb carbon dioxide present in the flask.

questions.enonce_markdown: During epigeal germination, the plumule and cotyledons are carried out of the soil. This is brought about by:
questions.corrige_markdown: In epigeal germination (for example bean, groundnut) the hypocotyl elongates and arches, pulling the cotyledons and the plumule up above the soil. In hypogeal germination it is the epicotyl that elongates, and the cotyledons stay underground. **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: Elongation of both hypocotyl and epicotyl.
Elongation of both plumule and radicle.

questions.enonce_markdown:
When a marine Amoeba is put in fresh water environment. It will,

*Options as printed:* A) Absorb much water swells and bursts.   B) Give off much water, become dehydrated and dies.   C) Develop a contractile vacuole to collect excess water.   D) Form pseudopodia and moves away.
questions.corrige_markdown: Fresh water is hypotonic to the cytoplasm of a marine Amoeba, so water enters by osmosis. Two answers are defensible: (A) an organism not adapted to fresh water absorbs water, swells and bursts; (C) a protozoan responds by using contractile vacuoles to collect and expel the excess water (marine forms have few or no active vacuoles, so they must form or speed up vacuoles). B is the opposite of what happens, and D has no link with osmosis. Because the printed question does not say which of A or C the examiner wants, it is left open for self-assessment. Most probable intended key: **C**.

questions.enonce_markdown: Excess chemical fertilizers from an industry were washed off by rain water into a pond. What was the effect on the organisms in the pond?
questions.corrige_markdown: Nitrates and phosphates from the fertilizers cause an algal bloom. When the algae die, bacteria decompose them and use up the dissolved oxygen (eutrophication), so fish and other aerobic organisms suffocate and die. Option D describes only the first stage (the algae) and not the effect on the organisms of the pond as a whole. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: They suffocated and died due to lack of oxygen.
They grew rapidly occupying other areas.
They were exposed to predators as the water became hot.

questions.enonce_markdown:
The graph below refers to the level of two hormones observed in blood within a month in a sixteen-year-old girl.

![fig-6](gce-ol-biology-2023-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_6.png)

The increase in the level of oestrogen between Day 13 and Day 15 is due to:
questions.corrige_markdown: The graph shows a sharp peak of oestrogen (solid line) at about day 14 of the cycle. This surge triggers a surge of LH, which causes ovulation, the release of the egg from the ovary. Thickening of the wall (A) happens before the peak and is caused by oestrogen, the corpus luteum (B) forms after ovulation and secretes progesterone (dotted line, peak about day 21), and menstruation (D) occurs at the start of the cycle when both hormones are low. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: Release of egg from the ovary.
Peeling off of the uterine wall.

questions.enonce_markdown: During vigorous activity there is overheating which results in much heat being lost through the skin. This is as a result of:
questions.corrige_markdown: When the body overheats, the arterioles in the skin dilate (vasodilation): more blood flows near the surface and more heat is lost by radiation, together with sweating. Vasoconstriction and shivering reduce heat loss or produce heat in the cold. Increased metabolism is the cause of the overheating, not of the heat loss through the skin. **Answer: D.**
